title: A Leader Shaped by God's Word

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When he takes the throne of his kingdom, he is to write for himself on a scroll a copy of this law, taken from that of the Levitical priests. It is to be with him, and he is to read it all the days of his life so that he may learn to revere the Lord his God and follow carefully all the words of this law and these decrees. - Deut 17:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a remarkable instruction. The king, the most powerful person in the land, was to personally write out his own copy of God's law and read it every day of his life. He was not above the Word; he was to sit under it daily. The purpose was tender and clear, that he might learn to revere the Lord and carefully obey Him.

Think about what this means. Power did not exempt the king from God's Word; it made his need of it greater. The higher his position, the more he needed the humbling, guiding influence of Scripture shaping his heart each day. A king who neglected God's Word would soon drift into pride and ruin.

This is a beautiful picture for every one of us. None of us is too important, too busy, or too mature to need God's Word daily. Reverence for God grows as we soak in what He has said. Jesus, our perfect King, lived entirely by the Word of God, answering every temptation with "It is written" (Matt 4:4). If the King of kings treasured Scripture, how much more do we need it? A daily, humble return to God's Word keeps our hearts soft and our lives on course. Is God's Word a daily companion for you, or an occasional visitor?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is God's Word a daily companion or an occasional visitor?
2. What keeps you from reading Scripture regularly?
3. How might daily time in the Word reshape your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a hunger for Your Word every single day. Let it humble me, guide me, and grow my reverence for You. Amen.
